title: first-watch adhoc routines and followups
content:
Quick first-watch scratchpad. Mostly for me; messy.

Summary of night pages I saw and immediate follow-ups:
- 2026-08-21 01:14 UTC: repeated 503s hitting /v1/generate on hosted (pager-1589).
  - Symptom: elevated 5xx rate from our lb to app behind envoy, surge in "deadline exceeded" on the worker pods.
  - Immediate action: scaled inference-worker pool by +2 replicas (kubectl scale deployment/inference-worker -n prod --replicas=14).
  - Result: error rate dropped ~65% within 4m but latency remained elevated for long-tail requests.
  - Pager note: set annotation on rollout to preserve logs: pager-1589 annotated.
  - Followups: check if autoscaler backpressure is mis-configured for burst windows (see TODO #1).

- 2026-08-21 03:02 UTC: alert on high EBS i/o wait for dedicated shard (dedicated-eu-west-2-03).
  - Symptom: slow checkpoint writes during model reloads, interfering with KV cache warmup.
  - Immediate action: disabled scheduled reloads on that shard, moved traffic to standby via routing tag.
  - Followups: open infra ticket to check disk health and snapshot schedule (JIRA:INFRA-1102).

Runbook TODOs (short actionable list):
- [ ] TODO #1: Autoscaler: re-evaluate target metrics for inference-worker HPA. Current config uses cpu-avg (50%) but we should add queue-concurrency metric. Add note / PR: GH:repo/infra#992.
- [ ] TODO #2: Add prewarm window to model reload runbook: add step to stagger reloads across shards and check EBS throughput. (confluence://runbooks/model-reloads)
- [ ] TODO #3: Update KB about 503->deadline exceeded mapping and mitigation steps for oncall runbook. Quick blurb under "traffic spikes" section.
- [ ] TODO #4: Create a lightweight test to reproduce long-tail latency under KV-cache misses (script: tools/loadtest/kv-miss-sim).

Notes-to-self (oncall habits and pointers):
- If 5xx blast coincides with a spike in unmatched prompts, check prefix-caching hitrate (dashboards: console -> model -> cache-hit-rate) before scaling too aggressively.
- When escalating to Platform, include tracer IDs from the first failing request (trace: 7a3f..).
- For dedicated customers, route incidents through cs-ops first (they have runbooks for shard failover).

Useful commands I ran / recommend leaving in runbook:
- kubectl -n prod logs deployment/inference-worker --tail=200 --since=10m | grep "deadline exceeded"
- kubectl -n prod exec -it svc/bench-client -- /bin/bash -c "python -m tools.load.kv_miss_sim --rps 200 --duration 120"
- aws ec2 describe-instance-status --instance-ids i-0123456789abcdef0 --region eu-west-2

Open questions / unresolved:
- Q1: Why did the autoscaler not spin up faster during the first 90s? HPA logs show scale event at +2m. Need to correlate with controller-manager events and check if kube-scheduler was CPU-bound (rare).
- Q2: Is there an upstream kernel/driver issue on the affected EBS host? Infra asked for iostat and snapshot history.

Signals / metrics to monitor after changes:
- 5xx rate by route (/v1/generate), 99th latency, queue-length on inference-worker, cache hit-rate, EBS avg await.

Postmortem sketch (notes to expand later):
- Trigger: traffic spike + cold-KV-cache misses on a shard with concurrent model reloads -> increased IO contention -> long-tail latencies -> downstream deadlines -> 503s.
- Immediate mitigations: scale workers, re-route traffic, disable reloads on affected shard.
- Longer term mitigation candidates: stagger reloads, add prewarm step, change HPA target metrics, add alert for "reload in progress" with ebs-iowait threshold.

Followups for next shift (assign or check):
- Jordan: check kube-controller-manager logs around 01:10-01:18 UTC and summarize why HPA reaction delayed. (linked INFRA ticket).
- Soren: AHV to run iostat and snapshot verification on dedicated-eu-west-2-03, follow-up in INFRA-1102.
- Me (Amelia): draft runbook amendments for model reloads and autoscaler remarks, open PR to infra repo with config suggestions.

Random ephemeral notes (scratch):
- Reminder: ping #sre-rotations about oncall overlap next month (I have a vacation block Aug 29 - Sep 2).
- Keep a short checklist in runbook: 1) confirm tracing id 2) check cache-hit 3) check ebs iowait 4) scale if queue>300

End-of-shift handoff blurb (to paste into rotation thread):
- "First-watch (Amelia): handled two pages -> pager-1589 (503s) and a disk iowait alert on dedicated shard. Immediate mitigations applied, follow-ups created (SRE-4231, INFRA-1102). See personal scratch doc for commands and TODOs. Leaving HPA investigation to Jordan."

-- Amelia

(rough, will clean up and push runbook PR after handoff)
